prose.title: The Hawks Had No Quarterback in April and Two by August
prose.dek: Chris Klingenberg sat still through the spring, then spent {{f.team.0012.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, {{f.team.0012.top_buy_price}} of it on Jared Goff. The preseason simulation has the Hawks {{f.team.0012.power_rank|ord}}, in a division with the league's top-ranked team.

paragraphs: April was bare. The Hawks carried {{f.team.0012.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0012.cap_opening}} in salary, and there was no quarterback on the roster at all, so Jakobi Meyers, a receiver, sat in the superflex. Kyren Williams, a High-end RB2, was the only solid starter, and there was not one top-twelve player at any position. The other {{f.team.0012.holes_opening}} spots were holes: nobody at quarterback, J.K. Dobbins at the second running back spot, Mike Evans and Michael Wilson at receiver, Dalton Kincaid at tight end, and RJ Harvey, Chimere Dike and Meyers in the flexes.

Then nothing, deliberately or not. No trade, no cut, no extension before the rookie draft. {{f.team.0012.expired_rookies}} rookie deals ran out and none was kept: Drew Sanders, Luke Schoonmaker and Nolan Smith simply left, and Jordan Battle went to L.A. Looks at the Expired Rookie Auction.

t.0012.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft was the whole pre-auction offseason, and it was a good one to have. The Hawks made {{f.team.0012.rookie_picks_count}} picks, two of them in the first round: Carnell Tate at 1.02, a slot that has produced a usable player half the time, and Makai Lemon at 1.06. Tate went straight into the lineup as a Low-end WR3. Kaelon Black, Ja'Kobi Lane, Drew Allar, CJ Allen and Mansoor Delane followed, and the two defenders, Allen and Delane, are already starting.

No Expired Rookie Auction buys, no tags, no cuts and no trades until the roster locked. Klingenberg carried {{f.team.0012.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0012.cap_preauction}} into the auction, plenty of room and a lot of it needed.

He spent it on quarterbacks. Jared Goff cost {{f.team.0012.faa_12611_price}} after twelve bids, the most contested of his wins, and Matthew Stafford {{f.team.0012.faa_9431_price}}. That is {{f.team.0012.faa_spend}} in all at the Free Agent Auction, with Rachaad White at {{f.team.0012.faa_15721_price}}, Rhamondre Stevenson at {{f.team.0012.faa_15259_price}} and Travis Kelce at {{f.team.0012.faa_11244_price}} behind them.

It bought two real starters. Stafford grades as a Low-end QB1 and Kelce as a Low-end TE1; Goff, a High-end QB2 in the superflex, is the Good in the What it bought column. White and Stevenson are depth. Measured against every owner's money, his money ranks {{f.team.0012.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added, and {{f.team.0012.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} for how much it added in all: the middle of the league on both counts, which for a team that started with no quarterback is a real summer.

Six of those buys went on multi-year contracts at the auction, and the biggest ones are long: Goff at {{f.team.0012.contract_12611_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0012.contract_12611_tcv}} in all, Stafford at {{f.team.0012.contract_9431_tcv}}, and White at {{f.team.0012.contract_15721_tcv}}. There were no restructures before, during or after it.

After the auction he traded a 2027 fourth to Real Deal Creel for George Karlaftis and a 2027 fifth, cut Marquise Brown with {{f.team.0012.cut_14105_salary}} of salary and a {{f.team.0012.cut_14105_penalty}} penalty charged to 2027, and claimed Cairo Santos and Sam Martin off waivers to kick and punt.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0012.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Stafford and Kelce, and {{f.team.0012.holes_today}} holes: Stevenson at the second running back spot, Mike Evans and Carnell Tate at receiver, and Michael Wilson and J.K. Dobbins in the flexes. Receiver is where the Hawks rank lowest, {{f.team.0012.wr_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}. The kicker, Andres Borregales, is an Elite PK1 on MFL's projections.

What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Klingenberg has been here since {{f.team.0012.hist_first_season}}, {{f.team.0012.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, and the record is honest about them: no title, one runner-up finish in {{f.team.0012.hist_runner_up_years}}, {{f.team.0012.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, and division titles in {{f.team.0012.hist_div_title_years}}. His career all-play record of {{f.team.0012.hist_allplay_pct}} is the lowest in the league.

DOG POUND 4 LIFE is C-Town Chivalry's division until someone takes it from them. The simulation ranks C-Town {{f.league.power_rank_0009|ord}} in the league with {{f.league.p_title_0009}} title odds, Cleon Ca$h {{f.league.power_rank_0011|ord}}, and the Hawks {{f.team.0012.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0012.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and a {{f.team.0012.sim_p_division}} chance at the division. Each of them is played five times.

The next three years, Klingenberg style. 2027: the Hawks win DOG POUND 4 LIFE?!?! Goff and Stafford carry it... no, wait, strike that, C-Town wins it, bro, but the Hawks make the playoffs. 2028: Tate is a lead receiver and Lemon is right behind him, and this is the year, dude, this is definitely the year. 2029: they do not win the title. Actually, they might. That is the projection, and he will have changed his mind about it twice by the time you read this.

Week one is off to a better start than the spring. With {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Mike Evans caught a touchdown, Kyren Williams ran one in, and the Hawks already have {{f.team.0012.wk_points_final}} points in the bank. Stafford threw an interception in a quiet first game.
